required_fixes.description: C3 (browser diff <106.7) and C4 (param workflow <= literal) are tautologically satisfied because producer computes both conditions' browser+verification cost from the SAME measured total (1498.113ms) added as constant offset. Literal and parameterized execute identical HTTP actions by design, so browser_cost difference is identically 0.0 and workflow difference identically 1067 tokens (parent arithmetic). Neither criterion can discriminate; they cannot falsify even if browser costs were huge. Frozen spec makes this degenerate, but producer interpretation treats passing C3/C4 as empirical evidence that browser costs 'do not dominate'.

required_fixes.fix: If differential browser cost is intended to be testable, measure browser execution independently per condition (e.g., separate registry selection paths, different URL-resolution code paths) or rephrase C3/C4 as consistency checks, not as falsifiers. Rename claim to 'browser costs are measurable and identical across conditions by construction' and bound inference accordingly.

required_fixes.description: C2 reports 32/32 tasks with verification_time_ms >0 (median 0.026ms/task, total 0.844ms). Measurement is json.loads + status check micro-benchmark in Python, not semantic verification (response schema, correctness). Values 0.003-0.05ms are near timer resolution and do not co-vary with body size as baselines expected (B-VERIFICATION-RESPONSE expected 'correlated with response body size' - observed 27KB body 0.205ms vs 2-byte 404 body 0.003ms shows weak correlation, 0.06% of total). Pass is technically correct per threshold but does not validate realistic verification cost.

validity_findings.finding: Browser execution uses Python requests library, not Playwright/Selenium real browser. Spec explicitly allows this ('via Python requests library with time.perf_counter()'), so compliant with frozen validity, but representation loss remains: real browser adds rendering, JS, navigation overhead that requests omits. Producer discloses (validity_notes). Since overhead would again be constant across conditions (same URLs), it would not change differential conclusion, but absolute workflow cost ceiling is understated.

validity_findings.finding: Token-equivalent conversion 1ms ~ 1 token used to compute browser_verification_pct_of_token_savings 140.5% (1499/1067) and to add to token counts. Producer correctly labels 'rough approximation' and notes key insight is identical offset preserves inequality regardless of rate. However report.md tables compare 'Token Cost | Browser+Verification | Total Workflow' by summing incompatible units (tokens + ms). At alternative rates (e.g., 0.1ms/token or 10ms/token) absolute totals shift dramatically; only ordering (param < literal) is invariant. 140.5% figure is conversion-dependent, not a physical ratio.

claim_ceiling: Browser and verification costs are measurable via Python requests to jsonplaceholder.typicode.com on the synthetic 32-task corpus (N=32, 3 runs median): total 1498ms browser +0.84ms JSON/status verification (~47ms/task, verification 0.06% of non-token cost). At 1ms~1 token this equals ~1499 token-equivalents (140% of the 1067-token analytical margin) but because the same HTTP actions are executed in LITERAL, PARAMETERIZED and COLD, the cost is a constant offset: arithmetic 18624+1498 <19691+1498 is preserved. This SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST per frozen decision rule C1-C5. No inference justified that 5.42% token savings is economically meaningful: parent token costs are analytical estimates (completion tokens 2/15/20) with unmeasured success rate (C1 100% assumed), browser measured is requests library not Playwright, verification is JSON parse only, endpoint is CDN not production, and COLD remains 5.1-5.3x cheaper (3974 vs 20123/21190) with unmeasured real success. C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS. Maximum justified claim: 'On synthetic 32-task corpus, browser+verification cost is non-zero, negligible verification, and identical across registry conditions by construction, so it does not differentially offset analytically-estimated token savings.' Do not generalize to real SPIDER corpus, real LLM completions, real browser, or production network.
